name: betterleaks-structured-partial-scan-diagnostics
instr:
betterleaks cannot expose partial, recoverable acquisition failures alongside completed findings. Build one ordered outcome across sources, detection, CLI policy, JSON, and SARIF without changing legacy finding APIs or reports.

Diagnostic-capable sources emit unwrap-compatible diagnostics with severity, acquisition stage, source kind, stable native target, message, and available cause; successful acquisition emits none. Files distinguishes walk, metadata, open, size, and permission outcomes, continuing eligible siblings by lexical path. Git distinguishes startup, stderr, parse, blob, and completion failures, retains earlier fragments, and classifies context cancellation as cancellation. GitHub, GitLab, HuggingFace, and S3 distinguish enumeration, download, delegated repository, and resource failures while preserving provider and nested identity.

Sequence every accepted finding or diagnostic uniquely in callback order. Drain validation before one terminal outcome. Filtering and diagnostics must not change finding status or counts. Preserve diagnostic sequence, source, and target through detection, CLI-generated JSON, and SARIF. Cancellation preserves accepted events, rejects later callbacks, and emits exactly one canceled outcome. A racing Git failure must still be classified correctly. Queued validation results and accepted diagnostics precede the terminal outcome even if the source returns an error.

`Detector.Run` and deprecated `Detector.DetectSource` keep existing findi
